questions.questionText: Which OSI layer is responsible for segmentation and end-to-end delivery using TCP and UDP?

explanation.correct: The Transport layer segments data and provides end-to-end delivery through TCP (reliable) or UDP (best effort).
explanation.incorrect: Layer 2 handles frames and MAC addressing, Layer 3 handles IP addressing and routing, and Layer 5 manages sessions.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.5 Compare TCP to UDP

questions.questionText: Which TCP/IP model layer corresponds to OSI Layers 5, 6, and 7?

explanation.correct: The TCP/IP Application layer combines the OSI Session, Presentation, and Application layers.
explanation.incorrect: Transport maps to OSI Layer 4, Internet to Layer 3, and Network Access to Layers 1 and 2.
explanation.examTip: TCP/IP has four layers: Application, Transport, Internet, Network Access.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.1 Explain the role and function of network components

questions.questionText: How many usable host addresses are available in the 10.1.1.0/27 network?

explanation.correct: A /27 leaves 5 host bits, giving 2^5 = 32 addresses; subtracting the network and broadcast addresses leaves 30 usable hosts.
explanation.incorrect: 32 is the total including network and broadcast, 62 would be a /26, and 28 is not a power-of-two result.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.6 Configure and verify IPv4 addressing and subnetting

questions.scenarioText: A host is configured with the IP address 192.168.10.77/26.
questions.questionText: What is the network address of the host?

explanation.correct: A /26 mask creates blocks of 64 addresses (0, 64, 128, 192); 77 falls in the 64 block, so the network address is 192.168.10.64.
explanation.incorrect: 192.168.10.0 is the block below, and .72 and .96 are not /26 boundaries.
explanation.examTip: Find the block size (256 minus the mask octet) and round down to a multiple.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.6 Configure and verify IPv4 addressing and subnetting

questions.scenarioText: A host is configured with the IP address 172.16.35.130/21.
questions.questionText: What is the broadcast address of the subnet?

explanation.correct: A /21 uses 255.255.248.0, so the third-octet block size is 8. The host's subnet is 172.16.32.0 to 172.16.39.255, and the broadcast address is 172.16.39.255.
explanation.incorrect: 172.16.35.255 and 172.16.32.255 are not the last address of the block, and 172.16.47.255 belongs to the next block.
explanation.examTip: For non-/24 prefixes, work in the interesting octet.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.6 Configure and verify IPv4 addressing and subnetting

questions.scenarioText: A network engineer must use 192.168.1.0/24 for subnets that need 100, 50, 25, and 10 hosts. The 100-host subnet has already been assigned 192.168.1.0/25.
questions.questionText: Which network should be assigned to the 50-host subnet to conserve address space and avoid overlap?

explanation.correct: The 100-host subnet needs a /25 and uses 192.168.1.0/25 (0-127). The 50-host subnet needs a /26 (62 hosts), and the next free boundary is 192.168.1.128/26.
explanation.incorrect: 192.168.1.64/26 overlaps the /25, a /25 wastes space for 50 hosts, and 192.168.1.100/26 is not on a /26 boundary.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.6 Configure and verify IPv4 addressing and subnetting

questions.questionText: What is the EUI-64 interface ID created from a MAC address of 0050.56AA.BBCC?

explanation.correct: EUI-64 splits the MAC, inserts FFFE in the middle, and flips the 7th bit of the first byte (00 becomes 02).
explanation.incorrect: Skipping the bit flip or placing FFFE at the end produces an incorrect interface ID.
explanation.examTip: EUI-64: split, insert FFFE, flip the 7th bit.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.8 Configure and verify IPv6 addressing and prefix

questions.questionText: Which IPv6 prefix is used for link-local unicast addresses?

explanation.correct: Link-local addresses are in FE80::/10 and are valid only on the local link.
explanation.incorrect: FC00::/7 is unique local, FF00::/8 is multicast, and 2000::/3 is global unicast.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.9 Compare IPv6 address types

questions.scenarioText: An IPv6 host must learn the MAC address of another host on the same link before sending a frame.
questions.questionText: Which NDP message does the host use to discover that neighbor's Layer 2 address?

explanation.correct: Neighbor Solicitation and Neighbor Advertisement messages replace ARP in IPv6 for resolving Layer 2 addresses.
explanation.incorrect: Router messages are used to discover routers and prefixes, and Echo Request tests reachability.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.9 Compare IPv6 address types

questions.questionText: Select ALL valid host addresses in the 192.168.1.64/27 subnet.

explanation.correct: The /27 subnet runs from 192.168.1.64 to 192.168.1.95; hosts are .65 through .94.
explanation.incorrect: 192.168.1.64 is the network address and 192.168.1.95 is the broadcast address.
explanation.examTip: First and last addresses are not usable hosts.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.6 Configure and verify IPv4 addressing and subnetting

questions.questionText: Select ALL address types that exist in IPv6.

explanation.correct: IPv6 uses unicast, multicast, and anycast addresses.
explanation.incorrect: IPv6 has no broadcast; multicast replaces it.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.9 Compare IPv6 address types

questions.questionText: Select ALL valid shortened forms of 2001:0DB8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001.

explanation.correct: Leading zeros may be dropped and one run of consecutive zero groups may be replaced by a double colon.
explanation.incorrect: The double colon can be used only once, and three colons are never valid.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.8 Configure and verify IPv6 addressing and prefix

questions.questionText: Select the TWO characteristics of single-mode fiber compared with multimode fiber.

options.text: Typically uses a laser light source

explanation.correct: Single-mode fiber has a very small core, uses lasers, and supports much longer distances.
explanation.incorrect: Multimode fiber has the larger core and commonly uses LEDs, and 100 meters is the limit for UTP copper.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.3 Compare physical interface and cabling types

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: TCP uses a three-way handshake to establish a connection.
UDP provides sequencing and retransmission of lost segments.
DNS queries typically use UDP port 53.
TFTP uses TCP.

explanation.correct: TCP is connection-oriented with a three-way handshake, DNS queries typically use UDP 53, and TFTP uses UDP.
explanation.incorrect: UDP is connectionless and does not provide sequencing or retransmission.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.5 Compare TCP to UDP

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: A collapsed core design combines the core and distribution layers.
The access layer connects end-user devices to the network.
A three-tier design is required for every network regardless of size.
The core layer is the main place to apply user-level security policies.

explanation.correct: Small campuses often use a two-tier collapsed core, and the access layer connects endpoints.
explanation.incorrect: Three-tier is used for larger networks, and policy is primarily applied at the distribution and access layers.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.2 Describe characteristics of network topology architectures

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: A /31 prefix can be used on point-to-point links.
The IPv6 address :: represents the unspecified address.
FF02::1 is the all-nodes multicast address.
An IPv6 router forwards packets with link-local destination addresses to other links.

explanation.correct: RFC 3021 allows /31 on point-to-point links, :: is unspecified, and FF02::1 is all-nodes. Link-local packets are not forwarded off the link.
explanation.incorrect: Link-local scope means routers will not route them.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.9 Compare IPv6 address types

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: 192.168.5.31/27 is a valid host address.
192.168.5.32/27 is a network address.
10.1.1.64/26 and 10.1.1.100/26 are in the same subnet.

explanation.correct: In a /27 the block 0-31 ends with the broadcast .31, .32 starts a new subnet, a /20 starting at 16 covers 16-31, and 10.1.1.64/26 covers .64-.127.
explanation.incorrect: 192.168.5.31 is the broadcast address of its /27.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.6 Configure and verify IPv4 addressing and subnetting

questions.questionText: Select the default port number for each protocol.

explanation.correct: SSH uses 22, Telnet uses 23, DNS uses 53, and a DHCP server listens on UDP 67.
explanation.incorrect: Port 443 is HTTPS and is not used by any of these protocols.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.5 Compare TCP to UDP

questions.questionText: Select the correct value for each subnetting question.

explanation.incorrect: Adjacent masks differ by one prefix bit and are easy to confuse.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.6 Configure and verify IPv4 addressing and subnetting

questions.questionText: Select the correct Ethernet cable type for each connection.

explanation.correct: Like devices (switch to switch, router to PC) use crossover without Auto-MDIX, unlike devices use straight-through, and console connections use rollover.
explanation.incorrect: Rollover cables are only for console connections.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.3 Compare physical interface and cabling types

questions.questionText: Place the PDU names in order as data is encapsulated from the Application layer down to the Physical layer.

explanation.correct: Data becomes a segment at the Transport layer, a packet at the Network layer, a frame at the Data Link layer, and bits at the Physical layer.
explanation.incorrect: Frames carry packets, not the other way around.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.1 Explain the role and function of network components

questions.questionText: Place the VLSM subnet allocation steps in the correct order.

orderItems.text: Assign the next available block to the next largest requirement
Verify there is no overlap between subnets
Sort the requirements from largest to smallest
Assign the first address block to the largest requirement
List the host requirements for each subnet

explanation.correct: VLSM assigns the largest subnets first so that blocks remain aligned and smaller subnets fit into the remaining space.
explanation.incorrect: Assigning small subnets first causes fragmentation and overlaps.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.6 Configure and verify IPv4 addressing and subnetting

questions.questionText: Drag each IPv6 address to its address type.

explanation.correct: 2000::/3 is global unicast, FE80::/10 is link-local, FC00::/7 is unique local, and FF00::/8 is multicast.
explanation.incorrect: FD and FC prefixes are unique local, not global.
explanation.examTip: Know the first hex digits: 2/3, FE80, FC/FD, FF.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.9 Compare IPv6 address types

questions.questionText: Drag each protocol to the TCP/IP model layer where it operates.

explanation.correct: HTTP and DNS are application protocols, TCP and UDP are transport protocols, IP and ICMP belong to the Internet layer, and Ethernet and 802.11 are Network Access technologies.
explanation.incorrect: ICMP is carried in IP packets and belongs to the Internet layer.
explanation.examTip: TCP/IP: Application, Transport, Internet, Network Access.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.1 Explain the role and function of network components

questions.questionText: What is the default VLAN on a Cisco switch to which all ports initially belong?

explanation.correct: All Cisco switch ports are members of VLAN 1 by default.
explanation.incorrect: VLAN 0 is reserved, VLAN 99 is a common management or native VLAN by convention only, and VLAN 1002 is a legacy reserved VLAN.
explanation.examTip: Default VLAN = 1 and it cannot be deleted.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.1 Configure and verify VLANs (normal range) spanning multiple switches

questions.questionText: Which IEEE standard defines VLAN trunking tags?

explanation.correct: IEEE 802.1Q inserts a 4-byte tag into Ethernet frames to identify the VLAN.
explanation.incorrect: 802.1X is port-based authentication, 802.3ad is link aggregation, and 802.1D is the original spanning tree.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.2 Configure and verify interswitch connectivity

questions.questionText: Which command assigns an access port to VLAN 20?

explanation.correct: The interface command 'switchport access vlan 20' places an access port in VLAN 20.
explanation.incorrect: The trunk native VLAN command applies to trunk ports, and the other commands are not valid IOS syntax.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.1 Configure and verify VLANs (normal range) spanning multiple switches

questions.scenarioText: Logs on two switches show CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH messages on the trunk between them.
questions.questionText: What is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: The native VLAN is configured differently on each end of the trunk
The trunk uses 802.1Q on both ends
The root bridge priority is too high
The VTP domain name is missing

explanation.correct: CDP reports a native VLAN mismatch when the two ends of a trunk have different native VLANs.
explanation.incorrect: Using 802.1Q on both ends is correct, and VTP or STP priority do not generate native VLAN mismatch messages.
explanation.examTip: Native VLAN must match on both trunk ends.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.2 Configure and verify interswitch connectivity

questions.questionText: In RSTP, which port role provides an alternate path to the root bridge and stays in the discarding state?

explanation.correct: An alternate port offers a backup path to the root bridge through a different switch and is blocked until needed.
explanation.incorrect: Designated ports forward toward segments, root ports forward toward the root, and disabled ports are administratively down.
explanation.examTip: Alternate = backup path to root; Backup = redundant path to same segment.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.5 Describe the need for and basic operations of Rapid PVST+ Spanning Tree Protocol

questions.scenarioText: Three switches have these bridge priority and MAC values: SW1 32769 / 0000.0C11.1111, SW2 32769 / 0000.0C22.2222, SW3 40961 / 0000.0C00.0001.
questions.questionText: Which switch becomes the root bridge?

options.text: The switch with the highest MAC address

explanation.correct: The root bridge has the lowest bridge ID, which is priority first and MAC address second. SW1 and SW2 tie on priority, and SW1 has the lower MAC address.
explanation.incorrect: SW3 has a lower MAC but a higher priority value, so it loses, and the highest MAC never wins.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.5 Describe the need for and basic operations of Rapid PVST+ Spanning Tree Protocol

questions.scenarioText: An engineer is configuring an EtherChannel between two switches using LACP.
questions.questionText: Which pair of channel-group modes will form an EtherChannel?

options.text: Desirable on one switch and active on the other
Active on one switch and passive on the other
On on one switch and active on the other

explanation.correct: LACP forms a channel when at least one side is active, and active/passive works.
explanation.incorrect: Two passive sides never initiate negotiation, 'on' does not negotiate and cannot pair with LACP, and desirable is PAgP.
explanation.examTip: LACP: active/active or active/passive. PAgP: desirable/desirable or desirable/auto.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.4 Configure and verify (Layer 2/Layer 3) EtherChannel

questions.questionText: Which 802.11 standard operates in both the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands?

explanation.correct: 802.11n can operate in both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz.
explanation.incorrect: 802.11a and 802.11ac are 5 GHz only, and 802.11b is 2.4 GHz only.
explanation.examTip: n = dual band; ax = 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E).

questions.questionText: Which protocol does a lightweight access point use to communicate with a wireless LAN controller?

explanation.correct: Lightweight APs build CAPWAP tunnels to the WLC for control and data traffic.
explanation.incorrect: GRE, VXLAN, and IPsec are tunneling or overlay technologies not used for AP-to-WLC communication.

questions.questionText: Select ALL RSTP port states.

explanation.correct: RSTP has three states: discarding, learning, and forwarding.
explanation.incorrect: Blocking and listening are original STP states combined into discarding in RSTP.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.5 Describe the need for and basic operations of Rapid PVST+ Spanning Tree Protocol

questions.questionText: Select the TWO benefits of using VLANs.

options.text: Logical grouping of users regardless of physical location
Elimination of the need for a Layer 3 device between VLANs

explanation.correct: VLANs segment broadcast domains and allow logical groupings independent of physical location.
explanation.incorrect: Inter-VLAN traffic still needs routing, VLANs do not change cable limits, and they do not encrypt traffic.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.1 Configure and verify VLANs (normal range) spanning multiple switches

questions.questionText: Select ALL settings that must match on member ports for an EtherChannel to form.

explanation.correct: Member interfaces must have consistent speed, duplex, switchport mode, and VLAN settings.
explanation.incorrect: Descriptions and hostnames have no effect on bundling.
explanation.examTip: Mismatches cause ports to be suspended.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.4 Configure and verify (Layer 2/Layer 3) EtherChannel

questions.questionText: Select ALL statements that are true about WPA3.

options.text: WPA3-Personal uses SAE instead of the PSK handshake

explanation.correct: WPA3 improves security with SAE, mandatory PMF, and a 192-bit mode for enterprise.
explanation.incorrect: TKIP belongs to WPA, and WEP is obsolete.

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: A trunk port can carry traffic for multiple VLANs.
An access port carries traffic for multiple tagged VLANs.
802.1Q adds a 4-byte tag to the frame.
Native VLAN traffic is tagged by default.

explanation.correct: Trunks carry multiple VLANs with 802.1Q tags. Access ports belong to one VLAN, and native VLAN traffic is untagged by default.
explanation.incorrect: Access ports do not tag frames.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.2 Configure and verify interswitch connectivity

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: All ports on the root bridge are designated ports.
A lower bridge priority makes a switch more likely to become the root bridge.
STP forwards on all redundant links at the same time within a VLAN.
PortFast is recommended on switch-to-switch trunk links.

explanation.correct: The root bridge has designated ports only, and lower priority wins root election. STP blocks redundant links to prevent loops, and PortFast is for edge ports.
explanation.incorrect: PortFast on switch uplinks can create temporary loops.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.5 Describe the need for and basic operations of Rapid PVST+ Spanning Tree Protocol

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: Autonomous APs are configured individually.
Lightweight APs use CAPWAP tunnels to a controller.
Cloud-based AP management requires an on-premises WLC.
Split-MAC architecture divides functions between the AP and the controller.

explanation.correct: Autonomous APs are standalone, lightweight APs depend on a WLC using CAPWAP, and split-MAC divides real-time and management functions. Cloud-based management does not need a local WLC.
explanation.incorrect: Cloud-managed APs are controlled through a cloud dashboard.
explanation.examTip: Autonomous, controller-based (split-MAC), and cloud-based are the three models.

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: LACP is an open standard.
PAgP is Cisco proprietary.
One end can use LACP and the other end can use PAgP.
An EtherChannel can combine ports of different speeds.

explanation.correct: LACP is IEEE standard and PAgP is Cisco proprietary; they cannot negotiate with each other, and bundle members must run at the same speed.
explanation.incorrect: Mixing protocols or speeds prevents the channel from forming.

questions.questionText: Select the show command that displays each item.

explanation.incorrect: The other commands show different information.

questions.questionText: Select the STP/RSTP port role that matches each description.

dropdowns.prompt: Every port on the root bridge
Port on a non-root switch with the best path to the root
RSTP port that is a discarding backup path to the root

explanation.correct: Root bridge ports are designated, each non-root switch has one root port, and alternate ports are backup paths.
explanation.incorrect: Each role has a specific purpose in loop prevention.
explanation.examTip: Every non-root switch has exactly one root port.

APs build CAPWAP tunnels to a WLC
APs are managed from a vendor-hosted dashboard

explanation.correct: Autonomous APs are standalone, controller-based APs use CAPWAP, and cloud-based APs are managed from the cloud.
explanation.incorrect: The architectures differ by where management is performed.

questions.questionText: Place the commands in the correct order to configure an access port in VLAN 20.

explanation.correct: Privileged EXEC is entered first, then global configuration, then the interface, and then the port mode and VLAN.
explanation.incorrect: Interface commands cannot be entered before selecting the interface.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.1 Configure and verify VLANs (normal range) spanning multiple switches

questions.questionText: Place the STP tiebreakers for choosing a root port in the order they are evaluated.

explanation.correct: A switch selects the root port by lowest root path cost, then lowest sender bridge ID, then lowest sender port priority, then lowest sender port ID.
explanation.incorrect: These are checked sequentially, only moving on when the previous value ties.
explanation.examTip: Cost, bridge ID, port priority, port ID.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 2.5 Describe the need for and basic operations of Rapid PVST+ Spanning Tree Protocol

questions.questionText: Drag each 802.11 standard to the frequency band it supports.

explanation.correct: 802.11b/g use 2.4 GHz, 802.11a/ac use 5 GHz, and 802.11n/ax support both bands.
explanation.incorrect: 802.11ac is 5 GHz only despite being newer than 802.11n.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 1.11 Describe wireless principles

questions.questionText: Drag each IOS command to the feature it configures.

explanation.correct: Access commands set the mode and VLAN, trunk commands set mode and allowed VLANs, and EtherChannel uses channel-group and port-channel interfaces.
explanation.incorrect: Allowed VLANs apply to trunks only.

questions.questionText: Which summary route most efficiently represents the four networks 192.168.0.0/24 through 192.168.3.0/24?

explanation.correct: Four contiguous /24 networks (third octet 0-3) are covered by 192.168.0.0/22.
explanation.incorrect: A /23 covers only two networks, and a /21 covers eight (including networks not needed).
explanation.examTip: Summarize by finding the common bits.

questions.scenarioText: An administrator must divide 192.168.50.0/24 into equal subnets of 16 addresses each.
questions.questionText: How many subnets are created and how many usable hosts does each subnet provide?

explanation.correct: Each subnet has 16 addresses, so a /24 splits into 16 subnets (a /28) with 14 usable hosts after removing network and broadcast.
explanation.incorrect: The other combinations correspond to a /27, a /29, or ignore the network and broadcast addresses.
explanation.examTip: /28 = 16 subnets of 14 usable hosts from a /24.

questions.questionText: What is the default administrative distance of a static route configured with a next-hop IP address?

explanation.correct: A static route to a next-hop address has an administrative distance of 1.
explanation.incorrect: 0 is directly connected, 90 is EIGRP, and 110 is OSPF.
explanation.examTip: Connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, RIP 120.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.1 Interpret the components of routing table

questions.questionText: Which command configures a static route to 10.2.0.0/16 using next hop 192.168.1.2?

explanation.correct: The syntax is ip route <network> <subnet mask> <next hop>.
explanation.incorrect: The second option reverses the arguments, the third uses a wildcard mask, and the last is a host OS command.
explanation.examTip: Static routes use subnet masks, not wildcard masks.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.3 Configure and verify IPv4 and IPv6 static routing

questions.questionText: Which command configures an IPv4 default route to the next hop 203.0.113.1?

explanation.correct: A default route uses network 0.0.0.0 and mask 0.0.0.0 followed by the next hop.
explanation.incorrect: The other commands use invalid syntax or reversed arguments.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.3 Configure and verify IPv4 and IPv6 static routing

questions.scenarioText: A router has Loopback0 1.1.1.1, GigabitEthernet0/0 10.0.0.2, and GigabitEthernet0/1 172.16.0.1. No router-id command is configured.
questions.questionText: Which value will the router use as its OSPF router ID?

explanation.correct: Without a manually configured router ID, OSPF prefers the highest IP address on a loopback interface.
explanation.incorrect: Physical interface addresses are only used if no loopback exists, and 0.0.0.0 is not valid.
explanation.examTip: Order: manual router-id, highest loopback IP, highest active physical IP.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.4 Configure and verify single area OSPFv2

questions.scenarioText: A router has these routes: 10.0.0.0/8 static via R1; 10.1.0.0/16 OSPF via R2; 10.1.1.0/24 OSPF via R3; 10.1.1.0/24 RIP via R4. It receives a packet for 10.1.1.20.
questions.questionText: Which next hop does the router use?

explanation.correct: The /24 routes are the longest matches for 10.1.1.20. Between OSPF (AD 110) and RIP (AD 120) for the same prefix, the lower AD wins, so R3 is used.
explanation.incorrect: R1 and R2 are less specific matches, and RIP via R4 loses to OSPF on administrative distance.
explanation.examTip: Longest prefix first, then AD, then metric.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.2 Determine how a router makes a forwarding decision by default

questions.scenarioText: Two routers share the 10.0.12.0/24 link in area 0, but show ip ospf neighbor shows nothing. One router uses a hello interval of 10 seconds and the other 5 seconds.
questions.questionText: What is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: The routers have different interface costs
The hello and dead timers do not match
The OSPF process IDs are different

explanation.correct: OSPF neighbors on a link must use matching hello/dead intervals, area, subnet, and authentication.
explanation.incorrect: Process ID is locally significant, descriptions are cosmetic, and cost differences do not prevent adjacency.
explanation.examTip: Remember: hello/dead, area, subnet/mask, authentication, stub flags.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.4 Configure and verify single area OSPFv2

questions.scenarioText: An engineer is configuring router-on-a-stick for VLAN 20 on a router subinterface.
questions.questionText: Which command associates subinterface GigabitEthernet0/0.20 with VLAN 20?

explanation.correct: Router-on-a-stick subinterfaces use encapsulation dot1Q <vlan-id>.
explanation.incorrect: switchport commands apply to switches, and the other commands are invalid.
explanation.examTip: Subinterface needs encapsulation before assigning an IP address.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.3 Configure and verify IPv4 and IPv6 static routing

questions.scenarioText: Hosts in VLAN 20 cannot reach their default gateway configured on R1 subinterface Gi0/0.20. The subinterface configuration is correct, but the switch port connected to R1 is an access port in VLAN 1.
questions.questionText: What is the most likely problem?

options.text: The switch port connected to R1 is not configured as a trunk
The router subinterface needs a routing protocol
The VLAN 20 hosts need a default VLAN of 1

explanation.correct: Router-on-a-stick requires an 802.1Q trunk between the switch and router so tagged VLAN traffic reaches the subinterfaces.
explanation.incorrect: A routing protocol is not needed for connected VLAN subnets, and OSPF is unrelated.
explanation.examTip: Router-on-a-stick: trunk on switch, subinterface per VLAN.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.3 Configure and verify IPv4 and IPv6 static routing

questions.scenarioText: A network team needs a vendor-neutral first hop redundancy protocol for multi-vendor routers.
questions.questionText: Which FHRP is an IETF open standard?

explanation.correct: Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP) is an open standard FHRP.
explanation.incorrect: HSRP and GLBP are Cisco proprietary, and STP is not an FHRP.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.5 Describe the purpose of first hop redundancy protocol

questions.questionText: Select ALL settings that must match for two OSPF routers to become neighbors on an Ethernet link.

options.text: IP subnet and mask on the link

explanation.correct: Neighbors must agree on area, timers, subnet, authentication, and stub area flags.
explanation.incorrect: The process ID is local and cost can differ per router.
explanation.examTip: Different costs are fine; different timers are not.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.4 Configure and verify single area OSPFv2

questions.questionText: Select ALL correct default administrative distances.

explanation.correct: Connected is 0, static is 1, and OSPF is 110.
explanation.incorrect: RIP is 120, and eBGP is 20.

questions.questionText: Select the TWO configuration items needed to enable IPv6 routing and addressing on a router interface.

explanation.correct: IPv6 routing must be enabled globally with ipv6 unicast-routing, and the interface needs an IPv6 address.
explanation.incorrect: The other commands are not valid IOS commands.
explanation.examTip: ipv6 unicast-routing is not on by default.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.3 Configure and verify IPv4 and IPv6 static routing

questions.questionText: Select ALL statements that are true about OSPF.

options.text: The default cost is based on interface bandwidth
OSPF uses hop count as its metric
OSPF hello packets are sent to the multicast address 224.0.0.5
OSPF is a link-state routing protocol

explanation.correct: OSPF is link-state, hellos use 224.0.0.5, and cost is bandwidth based.
explanation.incorrect: Hop count and distance-vector characteristics belong to RIP.
explanation.examTip: OSPF cost = reference bandwidth / interface bandwidth.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.4 Configure and verify single area OSPFv2

questions.questionText: Select ALL components shown in a routing table entry.

explanation.correct: Routing entries include the prefix, next hop, AD/metric, and exit interface.
explanation.incorrect: VLAN IDs and MAC addresses are Layer 2 concepts not stored in routes.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.1 Interpret the components of routing table

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: A static route has an administrative distance of 1.
The default route is 0.0.0.0/0.
Dynamic routing protocols require manual route updates.
Directly connected routes have an administrative distance of 0.

explanation.correct: Static routes have AD 1, the IPv4 default route is 0.0.0.0/0, and connected routes have AD 0. Dynamic protocols update automatically.
explanation.incorrect: Manual updates are a characteristic of static routing.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.1 Interpret the components of routing table

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: Single-area OSPFv2 commonly uses area 0.
A DR is elected on point-to-point links.
The default hello interval on Ethernet is 10 seconds.
On a multiaccess segment, the router with the highest priority becomes the DR.

explanation.correct: OSPF commonly uses area 0, hello defaults to 10 seconds on Ethernet, and the highest priority wins DR election. No DR is elected on point-to-point links.
explanation.incorrect: Point-to-point links do not need a DR.
explanation.examTip: Highest priority then highest router ID.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.4 Configure and verify single area OSPFv2

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: Router-on-a-stick uses subinterfaces.
The switch port connected to a router-on-a-stick router should be a trunk.
A Layer 3 switch needs ip routing enabled to route between SVIs.
Each subinterface must use the same IP address.

explanation.correct: Router-on-a-stick uses a trunk and subinterfaces, and Layer 3 switches require ip routing for SVI routing. Each subinterface needs an address in its own subnet.
explanation.incorrect: The same IP on multiple subinterfaces would overlap subnets.
explanation.examTip: One subinterface per VLAN, each with its own subnet.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.3 Configure and verify IPv4 and IPv6 static routing

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: The longest prefix match is chosen before administrative distance.
For the same prefix learned from different sources, the lower AD is preferred.
The metric is compared across different routing protocols to select the best route.
A /32 host route is preferred over a /24 route for that host.

explanation.correct: Routers pick the longest prefix first, then lower AD among identical prefixes, then lower metric within the same protocol.
explanation.incorrect: Metrics from different routing protocols are not comparable.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.2 Determine how a router makes a forwarding decision by default

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: ipv6 route 2001:DB8:2::/64 2001:DB8:1::2 is a valid IPv6 static route.
::/0 is the IPv6 default route.
ipv6 unicast-routing is enabled by default on Cisco routers.
A static route using a link-local next hop must also specify the exit interface.

explanation.correct: IPv6 static routes follow the ipv6 route syntax, ::/0 is the default route, ipv6 unicast-routing must be enabled, and link-local next hops require an exit interface.
explanation.incorrect: Link-local addresses are only unique per link, so the interface is needed.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.3 Configure and verify IPv4 and IPv6 static routing

questions.questionText: Select the default administrative distance of each route source.

explanation.correct: Connected is 0, static is 1, OSPF is 110, and RIP is 120.
explanation.incorrect: 90 is the AD for EIGRP internal routes.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.1 Interpret the components of routing table

questions.questionText: Select the IOS prompt that matches each CLI mode.

explanation.correct: > is user EXEC, # is privileged EXEC, (config)# is global configuration, and (config-if)# is interface configuration.
explanation.incorrect: The prompt suffix reveals the mode.
explanation.examTip: enable moves to privileged EXEC; configure terminal to global config.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.3 Configure and verify IPv4 and IPv6 static routing

questions.questionText: Select the OSPF command that matches each task.

dropdowns.prompt: Stop sending hellos out a LAN-facing interface

explanation.correct: These OSPF commands enable the process, advertise networks, set the router ID, and suppress hellos on LAN interfaces.
explanation.incorrect: ip ospf cost modifies the metric rather than any of these tasks.
explanation.examTip: The network command uses a wildcard mask.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.4 Configure and verify single area OSPFv2

questions.questionText: Select the wildcard mask for each prefix length.

explanation.correct: A wildcard mask is the inverse of the subnet mask: /24 = 0.0.0.255, /26 = 0.0.0.63, /30 = 0.0.0.3, and /22 = 0.0.3.255.
explanation.incorrect: Subtract each octet of the subnet mask from 255.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.4 Configure and verify single area OSPFv2

questions.questionText: Select the meaning of each route code displayed in show ip route.

explanation.correct: C is connected, L is local host route, O is OSPF, and S* is a static candidate default route.
explanation.incorrect: The asterisk marks a candidate default route.
explanation.examTip: Learn the legend at the top of show ip route.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.1 Interpret the components of routing table

questions.questionText: Place the OSPF neighbor states in the order they are reached.

explanation.correct: Neighbors progress from Down through Init, 2-Way, ExStart, Exchange, and Loading to Full.
explanation.incorrect: Exchange occurs after ExStart and before Loading.
explanation.examTip: Down, Init, 2-Way, ExStart, Exchange, Loading, Full.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.4 Configure and verify single area OSPFv2

questions.questionText: Place the commands in the correct order to configure router-on-a-stick for VLAN 20.

explanation.correct: The physical interface is enabled first, then the subinterface is created, VLAN encapsulation is set, and finally the IP address is assigned.
explanation.incorrect: The encapsulation must be set before the subinterface accepts an IP address.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.3 Configure and verify IPv4 and IPv6 static routing

questions.questionText: Place the steps a router uses to forward a packet in the correct order.

orderItems.text: De-encapsulate the frame to expose the IP packet
Receive the frame and verify the destination MAC address
Determine the next hop and exit interface
Forward the frame out the exit interface
Look up the destination IP in the routing table (longest prefix match)
Resolve the next-hop MAC address and build a new frame

explanation.correct: A router removes the Layer 2 header, performs the routing lookup, determines the next hop, and re-encapsulates before transmitting.
explanation.incorrect: A new frame cannot be built until the next hop is known.
explanation.examTip: Layer 2 header changes at every hop; Layer 3 stays the same.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.2 Determine how a router makes a forwarding decision by default

questions.questionText: Drag each IOS command to the feature it configures.

explanation.correct: Static routes use ip route, OSPF uses router ospf and network statements, and router-on-a-stick uses subinterfaces with dot1q encapsulation.
explanation.incorrect: Each command set belongs to only one feature.
explanation.examTip: Group commands by feature when studying.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 3.3 Configure and verify IPv4 and IPv6 static routing

questions.questionText: Which DHCP message does a server send in response to a client's DHCPDISCOVER?

explanation.correct: The DHCP process is Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge, and the server answers a Discover with an Offer.
explanation.incorrect: DHCPREQUEST is sent by the client, DHCPACK finalizes the lease, and DHCPRELEASE ends it.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.3 Explain the role of DHCP and DNS within the network

questions.questionText: Which NAT type maps many private addresses to a single public address by using unique port numbers?

explanation.correct: PAT, also called NAT overload, translates multiple inside hosts to one public IP using different source ports.
explanation.incorrect: Static NAT is one-to-one, dynamic NAT uses a pool of addresses, and NAT64 translates between IPv6 and IPv4.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.1 Configure and verify inside source NAT using static and pools

questions.scenarioText: Clients in VLAN 20 are not receiving IP addresses. The DHCP server is located on a different subnet reached through a Layer 3 switch that routes VLAN 20.
questions.questionText: Which command should be configured on the VLAN 20 interface to resolve this problem?

explanation.correct: Because DHCP discovers are broadcasts, a relay agent must forward them. ip helper-address makes the Layer 3 interface forward DHCP broadcasts to the server's unicast address.
explanation.incorrect: Snooping trust is a Layer 2 security setting, ip address dhcp makes the interface a client, and a pool would make the router the server.
explanation.examTip: DHCP server on another subnet = relay agent.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.6 Configure and verify DHCP client and relay

questions.scenarioText: An administrator wants a router to synchronize its clock with an internal time server.
questions.questionText: Which command configures a Cisco router as an NTP client that synchronizes with the server 10.1.1.1?

explanation.correct: The ntp server command points the device to an upstream time source.
explanation.incorrect: ntp master makes the device a time source itself, and the others are not valid ways to set a server.
explanation.examTip: ntp server = client; ntp master = server.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.2 Configure and verify NTP operating in a client and server mode

questions.scenarioText: A router is configured with the command logging trap errors.
questions.questionText: Which syslog messages are sent to the syslog server?

explanation.correct: Logging trap errors sends the specified level and all more severe levels: emergencies, alerts, critical, and errors (0-3).
explanation.incorrect: Levels 4 and above (warnings, notices, informational, debug) are not sent.
explanation.examTip: Lower number = more severe; the trap level includes all lower numbers.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.5 Describe the use of syslog features including facilities and levels

questions.questionText: Select the TWO true statements about SNMP.

options.text: SNMP traps are unsolicited notifications sent by managed devices

explanation.correct: SNMPv3 adds security features, and traps are sent by agents without being polled.
explanation.incorrect: SNMPv2c sends community strings in clear text, and GET only reads values.
explanation.examTip: SET modifies; GET reads; trap notifies.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.4 Explain the function of SNMP in network operations

questions.questionText: Select the TWO true statements about QoS tools.

options.text: Policing buffers traffic to delay it
Shaping drops all excess traffic immediately
Policing drops or re-marks traffic that exceeds a configured rate
Shaping buffers excess traffic to smooth the rate

explanation.correct: Policing enforces a rate by dropping or re-marking, while shaping delays excess traffic using a buffer.
explanation.incorrect: The incorrect options swap the behaviors of policing and shaping.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.7 Explain the forwarding per-hop behavior (PHB) for QoS

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: A DHCP server listens on UDP port 67.
DNS can use TCP for zone transfers.
DNS maps MAC addresses to IP addresses.
DHCP uses TCP port 68.

explanation.correct: DHCP servers listen on UDP 67, and DNS uses TCP for large responses and zone transfers. DNS maps names to IP addresses, and DHCP uses UDP.
explanation.incorrect: ARP maps IP to MAC; DNS maps names to IP.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.3 Explain the role of DHCP and DNS within the network

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: An inside local address is the private address of an internal host.
An inside global address is the public address that represents an inside host.
PAT uses port numbers to distinguish sessions.
Static NAT maps many inside hosts to one public address.

explanation.correct: NAT terminology: inside local is private, inside global is public, PAT uses ports, and static NAT is one-to-one.
explanation.incorrect: Many-to-one translation is PAT.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.1 Configure and verify inside source NAT using static and pools

questions.questionText: Select the NAT type that matches each description.

dropdowns.prompt: One private address maps to one public address permanently
Private addresses map to public addresses from a pool as needed
Many private hosts share one public address using ports

explanation.correct: Static NAT is permanent one-to-one, dynamic NAT uses a pool, and PAT shares one address using ports.
explanation.incorrect: Each NAT type differs in how addresses are allocated.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.1 Configure and verify inside source NAT using static and pools

questions.questionText: Place the syslog severity levels in order from most severe (0) to least severe (7).

explanation.correct: The levels from 0 to 7 are Emergency, Alert, Critical, Error, Warning, Notice, Informational, Debug.
explanation.incorrect: Lower numbers are more severe.
explanation.examTip: Mnemonic: Every Awesome Cisco Engineer Will Need Icecream Daily.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.5 Describe the use of syslog features including facilities and levels

questions.questionText: Drag each protocol to the IP service category that best describes it.

explanation.correct: SSH and SNMP are used to manage devices, NTP and syslog support time synchronization and logging, and DHCP and DNS provide address and name services.

explanation.examTip: Know the purpose of each protocol.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.3 Explain the role of DHCP and DNS within the network

questions.questionText: Which element of the CIA triad does encryption primarily support?

explanation.correct: Encryption keeps data private so only authorized parties can read it.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 5.1 Define key security concepts (threats, vulnerabilities, exploits, and mitigation techniques)

questions.scenarioText: An administrator wants to disable Telnet access to a router while allowing remote management.
questions.questionText: Which command under line vty configuration restricts remote access to SSH only?

explanation.correct: transport input ssh allows only SSH for incoming vty connections and blocks Telnet.
explanation.incorrect: transport output controls outgoing sessions, login block-for is brute-force protection, and crypto key generate creates keys but does not restrict protocols.
explanation.examTip: SSH needs hostname, domain name, RSA keys, and a local user.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 4.8 Configure network devices for remote access using SSH

questions.scenarioText: A switch port is configured with switchport port-security maximum 1 and uses the default violation mode.
questions.questionText: What happens to the port when a second MAC address is learned?

options.text: The port enters the err-disabled state
The second device is allowed because the limit is ignored
The port drops only the second device's frames and stays up
The port converts to a trunk

explanation.correct: The default violation mode is shutdown, so the port goes err-disabled when the maximum number of MAC addresses is exceeded.
explanation.incorrect: Dropping frames while staying up is protect or restrict mode, and the maximum is not ignored.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 5.7 Configure and verify Layer 2 security features (DHCP snooping, DAI, port security)

questions.questionText: Which command permits the 192.168.10.0/24 network in a standard numbered ACL 10?

explanation.correct: Standard ACLs use numbers 1-99 and wildcard masks.
explanation.incorrect: 110 is an extended ACL number, subnet masks are not used in ACL source matching, and ip access-group applies an ACL to an interface.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 5.6 Configure and verify access control lists

questions.scenarioText: An administrator must block host 10.1.1.10 from reaching TCP port 80 on server 172.16.1.5 but allow all other traffic.
questions.questionText: Where should the ACL be placed?

options.text: As close to the destination as possible
On the web server interface only
As close to the source as possible

explanation.correct: Extended ACLs filter by source, destination, and port, so they are placed close to the source to block unwanted traffic early.
explanation.incorrect: Standard ACLs are placed close to the destination because they filter only by source address.
explanation.examTip: Extended near source; standard near destination.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 5.6 Configure and verify access control lists

questions.scenarioText: ACL 10 contains: 1) permit 10.1.1.0 0.0.0.255, 2) deny host 10.1.1.10. The ACL is applied inbound.
questions.questionText: What happens to a packet from host 10.1.1.10?

options.text: It is dropped by the implicit deny

explanation.correct: ACLs are processed top-down and the first match is used, so entry 1 permits the entire subnet before entry 2 is evaluated.
explanation.incorrect: Entry 2 is never reached for this host, and the implicit deny only applies if nothing matches.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 5.6 Configure and verify access control lists

questions.scenarioText: An access switch connects users to a distribution switch that leads to the corporate DHCP server. DHCP snooping is being enabled.
questions.questionText: Which ports should be configured as trusted?

options.text: Only the uplink toward the legitimate DHCP server
Only ports with static IP devices

explanation.correct: DHCP snooping trusts only ports leading to authorized DHCP servers, such as uplinks.
explanation.incorrect: User-facing ports are untrusted so rogue DHCP server messages are dropped.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 5.7 Configure and verify Layer 2 security features (DHCP snooping, DAI, port security)

questions.questionText: Select ALL threats mitigated by DHCP snooping and Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI).

explanation.correct: DHCP snooping blocks rogue DHCP servers, and DAI blocks forged ARP messages.
explanation.incorrect: Port scans and brute-force attacks are not mitigated by those features.
explanation.examTip: DAI uses the DHCP snooping binding table.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 5.7 Configure and verify Layer 2 security features (DHCP snooping, DAI, port security)

questions.questionText: Select ALL true statements about port security violation modes.

options.text: Protect puts the port into err-disabled state
Protect drops offending frames without notification
Restrict drops offending frames and generates logs and counters
Shutdown places the port in err-disabled state

explanation.correct: Shutdown disables the port, restrict drops and logs, and protect silently drops frames.
explanation.incorrect: Protect and restrict keep the port up.

metadata.examObjective: 200-301 5.7 Configure and verify Layer 2 security features (DHCP snooping, DAI, port security)

questions.questionText: Select ALL components of AAA.
